title: Spirit is true God; proceeds from Father and Son; Cap. 23 COMPLETE
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR, On creation in general, follows. I desire ye matter to be dispatched in as few words as possible — whenever it occurs that same one must treat belonging toward ye Trinity. plus not fetch upon himself troublesome plus perplexed disputations more greedily than stands as fitting, as Calvin Institutes 1.13.19 piously plus prudently warns, plus Twisse: — let ye reader set a limit to curiosity. 1 John 5:7. 15:26; John 14:16,26; 61:1; Fourthly, ye Holy Spirit stands as distinguished out from Father plus Son not only according to name but also according to hypostasis — Isaiah 48:16; XVIII. But ye difference between generation plus procession consists in ye mode belonging toward production. XVI. so ye Spirit stands as spirated out from eternity out from both — for just as ye Son stands as generated out from eternity out from ye Father. 20:22. And that same ye same proceeds out from ye Son — John 16:7; XV. Thirdly, that same ye Holy Spirit proceeds out from ye Father — John 15:26. XIV. Secondly, that same ye Holy Spirit stands as true God ye divine names, divine attributes, divine works, plus divine worship show. VI.
pass_b_english: VI. Secondly, that the Holy Spirit is true God the divine names, divine attributes, divine works, and divine worship show. XIV. Thirdly, that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father — John 15:26. XV. And that the same proceeds from the Son — John 16:7; 20:22. For just as the Son is generated from eternity from the Father, so the Spirit is spirated from eternity from both.

XVI. But the difference between generation and procession consists in the mode of production. XVIII. Fourthly, the Holy Spirit is distinguished from Father and Son not only according to name but also according to hypostasis — Isaiah 48:16; 61:1; John 14:16,26; 15:26; 1 John 5:7.

Let the reader set a limit to curiosity, and not fetch upon himself troublesome and perplexed disputations more greedily than is fitting, as Calvin Institutes 1.13.19 piously and prudently warns, and Twisse: whenever it occurs that one must treat of the Trinity, I desire the matter to be dispatched in as few words as possible. CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR, On creation in general, follows.
source_text: VI. Secundo, Spiritum sanctum esse verum Deum ostendunt nomina divina, attributa divina, opera divina, cultus divinus. XIV. Tertio, Spiritum sanctum procedere a Patre — Joh. XV.26. XV. Procedere vero eundem a Filio — Joh. XVI.7; XX.22. Sicut enim Filius ab aeterno ex Patre generatur, ita Spiritus ab aeterno ab utroque spiratur. XVI. Discrimen vero inter generationem et processionem in modo productionis consistit. XVIII. Quarto, Spiritus sanctus non solum secundum nomen, sed et hypostasin a Patre et Filio distinguitur — Isa. XLVIII.16; LXI.1; Joh. XIV.16,26; XV.26; I Joh. V.7. Modum curiositati imponat lector, nec molestas et perplexas disputationes cupidius quam par est sibi accersat, ut pie prudenterque monet Calvinus Inst. I.13.19, et Twissus: quoties de Trinitate disserendum occurrit, cupio rem expediri quam fieri potest paucissimis. CAPUT VICESIMUM QUARTUM, De creatione in genere, sequitur.
